classes.name: Warrior
classes.description: A durable, hard-hitting frontline fighter who uses Rage, stances and weapon mastery.
strengths: Can serve as either a tank or damage dealer.
Strong sustained damage against multiple melee targets.
Brings class-specific group buffs and debuffs.
limitations: Has limited tools for recovering after taking heavy damage.
soloTips: Plan recovery between difficult fights; Warriors have limited self-recovery tools.
groupUtility: Provides distinctive group buffs and debuffs.

classes.name: Paladin

specializations.name: Holy
specializations.focus: Single-target healing, group support and spell-focused damage.

specializations.name: Retribution
specializations.focus: Weapon attacks blended with Holy damage.

classes.description: A versatile champion whose Seals and Judgements support melee combat, healing and protection.
strengths: Holy supports single-target healing, group support and spell-focused damage.
Protection develops threat, mana and survival tools.
Retribution blends weapon attacks with Holy damage.

classes.name: Hunter
classes.description: A ranged fighter supported by a loyal pet, with options built around precision, traps and melee tools.
strengths: Pets gain broader ability access, family abilities and gear scaling.
Traps can be used during combat.
soloTips: A pet-focused specialization is available; the source does not rank leveling builds.
groupUtility: Ranged damage and a combat toolkit that includes traps.

classes.name: Rogue
classes.description: A precise combatant who uses stealth, control, poisons and weapon attacks to create openings.
strengths: Forever updates expand poison use and weapon options.
Specialization paths support daggers, other weapon types, finishers, bleeds and combat tricks.

classes.name: Priest
classes.description: A cloth-wearing spellcaster who supports allies with healing and buffs or turns to damaging magic.
strengths: Supports allies through buffs and healing.
Holy and Discipline include healing tools; Shadow provides a damage path.
limitations: Wears cloth armor and has few ways to escape enemies.
soloTips: Limited escape tools make positioning and avoiding unwanted enemies useful considerations.
groupUtility: Healing and buffs strengthen party members.

classes.name: Shaman
classes.description: An adaptable elemental combatant whose totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
strengths: Can deal melee or spell damage and heal.
Mail armor and shields contribute to its sturdier class toolkit.
limitations: The official overview describes limited crowd control.
groupUtility: Totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
Can fill damage or healing roles.

classes.name: Mage
classes.description: A fragile ranged spellcaster who chooses among Arcane, Fire and Frost tools.
strengths: Offers ranged single-target and area damage.
Polymorph provides crowd control.
Can provide party buffs and conjured food and water.
limitations: Fragile when caught in melee combat.
soloTips: Frost offers combat control; the official overview does not rank a leveling build.
groupUtility: Polymorph, party buffs, and conjured food and water.

classes.name: Warlock
classes.description: A spellcaster who combines Shadow and Fire magic with demonic allies.
strengths: Forever specializations support damage-over-time, demon synergies, and Shadow/Fire combinations.
Pets scale with their master’s stats.
limitations: Physically weak and relies on demon pets for protection.
soloTips: Demon pets can help protect the Warlock; no comparative leveling ranking is published here.

classes.name: Druid
classes.description: A nature-focused class with adaptable forms and distinct spellcasting, melee and healing paths.
strengths: Feral supports form-based melee and tanking approaches.
Balance provides a spellcasting damage path.
Restoration focuses on healing.
groupUtility: Can approach combat through damage, tanking or healing paths.

specialAccess: Skyborne characters and the Zephras Isle starting experience require the Heroic Pack or higher.
classNotes: Specialization roles and Forever identities are drawn from linked Blizzard deep-dives. Enhancement Shaman also has a dedicated, current Forever leveling and combat guide. Other class pages remain concise reference pages until class-specific play guides are researched.
buildProfileNote: No complete, version-verified talent loadouts have been published in this guide yet. Use specialization pages as sourced class overviews; do not treat them as point-by-point builds.

strengths: High single-target burst once the core talents come online.
Strong area damage becomes available early.
Self-healing helps recover after difficult pulls.
Ghost Wolf supports travel; the leveling guide calls out improved mobility after level 20.
weaknesses: Mana is a frequent constraint, especially before sustain talents.
Weapon upgrades matter greatly to melee damage.
The opening levels can feel slower before Stormstrike.
Several enemies at once can overwhelm the build.

talentMilestones.name: Shamanistic Focus
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide calls this out for reducing Shock mana costs; it does not publish a rank in the text.

talentMilestones.name: Stormstrike
talentMilestones.note: The guide recommends reaching the Enhancement core around this point and describes an optional respec at 25.

talentMilestones.name: Improved Stormstrike
talentMilestones.note: The guide marks this as a Mana-sustain and cooldown-reset pickup; it does not publish a rank in the text.

talentMilestones.name: Windfury Weapon
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide identifies this as a major power spike at level 30; use Rockbiter Weapon before then.

talentMilestones.name: Mindfulness
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide recommends returning to Restoration for additional passive Mana sustain.

talentMilestones.name: Water Shield
talentMilestones.note: The guide lists this as a further Mana return option.

levelingRotation.title: Keep ready
items: Before level 30, use Rockbiter Weapon; from level 30, the leveling guide recommends Windfury Weapon.
Place only the totems useful for the next fight; totems stay where placed.

levelingRotation.title: During a pull
items: Use a low-rank Lightning Bolt to pull a distant enemy when helpful.
Use Stormstrike on cooldown once learned; respond to Improved Stormstrike resets once talented.
Use Earth Shock for damage or to interrupt a spellcaster.
Use Flame Shock on multiple enemies; use Frost Shock when threat is a concern.
Use Fire Nova when a Fire Totem is active and Mana allows; otherwise keep attacking.
Heal with Healing Wave after a pull and drink when Mana is low.

singleTargetRotation: Keep Magma Totem active; use Searing Totem when Mana is tight.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented, for priority targets or a planned burst window.
Use Stormstrike on its six-second cycle.
Cast Lightning Bolt when Maelstrom Weapon reaches five stacks; avoid spending fewer stacks because it can reset the swing timer.
Use Earth Shock; use Fire Nova with a Fire Totem active when Mana permits.
aoeRotation: Keep a Fire Totem active and use Fire Nova on its cycle.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented.
Use Stormstrike and Earth Shock between Fire Nova casts.
Spend Maelstrom Weapon at five stacks when talented.
AoE is Mana intensive; reduce optional casts when resources run low.
precombat: Use the recommended weapon imbue for your level/build.
For a group, the guide lists Strength of Earth, a Fire Totem, Mana Spring, and Windfury Totem as the baseline set; trade Magma for Searing if Mana is limited.
utility: Strength of Earth Totem for group Strength; Stoneskin Totem when physical defense matters.
Windfury Totem for groups; Grounding Totem against spellcasters.
Earthbind Totem for slowing nearby threats; Tremor Totem for Fear, Charm, and Sleep.
Totemic Recall can recover Mana when moving and replacing totems.
Healing Wave for efficient recovery between pulls.
levelingStats: Weapon DPS first; prefer a slow two-handed weapon (the guide suggests approximately 3.3–3.8 speed).
Intellect for Mana and talent scaling.
Strength for melee damage, especially before Intellect scaling improves.
Spirit becomes more useful for Mana sustain after Improved Stormstrike or Mindfulness.
Agility and Stamina are situational secondary choices.
endgameStats: Weapon DPS, Hit Chance, Expertise, Intellect, Strength, then Spell Power.

quests.name: Call of Earth
quests.reward: Earth Totem; the Dwarf route also lists Stoneskin Totem.
quests.note: The level 4 details cited are for Dwarf Shaman; other race routes differ.

quests.name: Call of Fire
quests.reward: Fire Totem; the Dwarf route lists Searing Totem.
quests.note: Icy Veins says this can be picked up from any Shaman Trainer.

quests.name: Call of Water
quests.note: The guide recommends fitting this longer travel chain between other quests.

quests.name: Call of Air
quests.note: The leveling guide says this involves a Razorfen Kraul run and travel through multiple zones; race-specific details vary.

level60Builds.name: Standard Level 60 PvE
level60Builds.summary: Stormstrike and Improved Stormstrike form the core; the source also recommends Maelstrom Weapon, Rage of the Farseer, and Elemental picks including Elemental Devastation and Trial by Fire. Improved Ghost Wolf is optional; the source suggests two Tidal Focus points if skipped.
alternatives: Windfury Weapon is the source’s default imbue. Rockbiter may be preferable if Totem mechanics favor it; this remains unresolved in the source.
A Flametongue dagger setup is described as a possibility, not a verified recommendation.

level60Builds.name: Solo and small-group Level 60
level60Builds.summary: Trades deep Enhancement talents Maelstrom Weapon and Rage of the Farseer for more Mana sustain through Mindfulness while retaining Trial by Fire.
alternatives: The source frames this as an option when Judgement of Wisdom support is unreliable and Mana is a problem.
